$comment: One lifecycle spec, two executors: ui/src/lib/lifecycle.corpus.test.ts (the viewer's lifecycleAt) and crates/darkmux-serve/src/runs.rs's lifecycle_corpus test (the daemon's session fold). Each case is the records of one or more runs, an as-of instant (both executors judge the records at or before it; an untimed record is always in), the run judged (`run`: a session and optionally a mission, which the daemon reads as `/runs` reads that mission's row, by its own attempts on the session; absent, the session a `#dispatch=<id>` link names, as the session's current run), and the phase and status every surface must state for it then. A case the daemon cannot judge says why in server_skip_reason; the only such input is session presence.

cases.name: a started run is open
a run silent for exactly the window is still open
a run silent past the window has stopped with no ending recorded
a completed run is closed
a watchdog kill is an error
a presence reconciler close ends the run with no ending recorded
a terminal whose timestamp does not parse still closes the run
a terminal timestamped before its own start (clock skew) closes the run
before its start a run has not started
a close after the as-of instant does not close it yet
a budget wait before any start is waiting until its resume time
a budget wait is never stale before its resume time plus the grace
past its resume time plus the grace a lapsed wait is open, its staleness clock running from there
a lapsed wait silent past the window has stopped
a resumed wait is an ordinary open run
a wait the operator stopped closes the run as aborted
a stopped wait that names no reason ends with no ending recorded
a running dispatch the pacer held, then stopped, is closed
a start after a stopped wait opens the run again
a relaunch under the same session id after a clean finish is open
a relaunch supersedes an attempt that never closed; the new attempt closes on its own terminal
presence holds a silent run open
presence does not reopen a closed run
records with no opening are not a run
a mission's lifecycle session closes on mission.close
a run.error after a mission.close is the outcome over the close
a mission aborted by the operator is abandoned as aborted
before its wait is announced a held call has not started
a wait re-announced at its resume time waits to the new resume time
a terminal ends a wait
a mission-less session.end in a shared session closes the run open at its time
the same mission-less session.end leaves the earlier mission's clean finish alone
the later mission's run owns the mission-less close
before the mission-less close the later mission's run is open
an earlier mission's run silent past the window reads stopped beside a later mission on its session
a later mission starting on a shared session does not stop an earlier mission's run still in flight
presence holds open only the session's current run, not an earlier mission's
presence holds the session's current run open
presence never opens a run that has not started
a dispatch terminal is the outcome even when a session.end closed the run first
a close with nothing opened is not a run, but its session reads as ended
a mission's session whose only record is its recorded end reads as ended for that mission
a dispatch terminal with nothing opened is not a run, but reads as its outcome
with nothing opened, a dispatch terminal is the recorded outcome over an earlier session.end
a budget.resume in the same second as its wait ends the wait
a relaunch does not inherit the earlier attempt's budget wait
a terminal from a skewed clock that arrives before its start closes the run
a mission-less session.end closes the run still open at its time, not a later mission's finished one
a mission-less session.end after a later mission's clean finish leaves that finish alone
skewed closes from before every start are placed in time order: a mission's own close beats a later mission-less one
an untimed opener mid-stream is segmented after every timed record
a run's own session is open from its run.start
a run.complete closes the run as complete
a run.error closes the run as an error
a run's own session silent past the window has stopped with no ending recorded
a run terminal is the outcome even when a session.end closed the run first
a second run.start on a run session after its close opens the next attempt
a close names its own execution: the sibling that started later is still open
the latest execution's own complete closes it, whatever order the executions ended in
a resumed execution's second start opens the next attempt of the same execution
a task's last step.complete closes its session
a step.complete with a later step still planned leaves its task's session open
the first bookend terminal is the outcome over a later one
a step that starts after its task's dispatch finished opens the next attempt
a skewed terminal naming its mission closes that mission's run on a shared session
a skewed terminal naming another mission leaves this mission's run open
an execution the operator stopped (its terminal names the stop) is aborted, not an error
